style:
STYLE GUIDE (apply to every asset):
Top-down 3/4 perspective pixel art for a 2D mystery/investigation game, in the readable, cozy-clean style of classic farming/life-sim pixel games, but dark and atmospheric.
Setting: an original foggy Victorian-era industrial world with occult undertones: cobblestone streets, gas lamps, soot-stained brick, wrought iron, canals, chapels, secret societies, alchemical potions.
Grid: strict 16x16 pixel tiles. Overworld characters are 16x32 pixels per frame. Every pixel must align to the grid; no half pixels, no sub-pixel detail.
Pixels: crisp hard-edged pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients; deliberate 2-tone checker dithering only on large surfaces or for fake transparency. 1px dark outline in deep blue-grey (around #1a1c2c, not pure black) on characters, props and icons; terrain tiles have no outline.
Palette: limited muted palette of max 32 colors, matching the existing game sprites. Desaturated slate blues, fog greys, soot browns, mossy greens, rust and brass, bone white; warm amber/yellow only for gas lamp light and candles; turquoise #6fe0d0 or deep violet reserved for occult/supernatural things. Avoid saturated primaries and pure black/white.
Lighting: flat base colors with 2-3 shade steps; light from top-left. Do not bake night darkness into sprites (the engine adds lighting).
Mood: melancholic, mysterious, slightly unsettling, never gory.
Output: transparent background (PNG with alpha) unless stated otherwise, orthographic, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, no signature.
Avoid: 3D render look, painterly style, photorealism, chibi exaggeration, anime eyes, references to existing games, films or franchises.

ASSET: Boss battle sprite concept, single creature, side view facing LEFT, idle stance, full body, feet on a flat ground line at the bottom. 'Weichenfresser' (Switch-Eater): an elder, larger relative of the reference lantern-headed rail hound, but it has eaten iron for too long. Bigger, heavier, hunched, damaged. Instead of a lantern head it has a long heavy rusted jaw like a railway buffer/coupling, the rust maw slightly open with small amber sparks glowing in its throat. Its ribs are curved railway switch blades (Weichenzungen) bursting outward along its flank like a cage, rusty iron plates, broken rivets, bent rail pieces as spine spikes, four thick iron-and-sinew legs. Colors: rust brown, soot brown, iron slate grey, dull brass, a little amber only in the sparks. Chunky readable pixel art, about 90 pixels wide sprite scaled up 10x with perfectly square pixel blocks. Background: completely flat solid magenta #ff00ff, no shadow, no floor, nothing else.

ASSET: Boss battle sprite concept, wide composition, side view facing LEFT, idle, full body on a flat ground line at the bottom. 'Tiefenvorarbeiter' (Deep Foreman): the relative of the reference living mine-gallery rock mass, but here it has risen up as a hulking, stooped mine foreman made of layered stratified rock and old timber pit props, wider than tall, heavy shoulders, long arms reaching the ground. His head is a battered miner's helmet with a lit brass pit lamp glowing amber in front, no visible face below it, just shadow. A long clay pipe in the shadow of the face, a thin wisp of smoke. Around his neck and across his chest hangs a long rusty chain full of small round brass shift tokens (tally tags). Cracked rock body with dark tunnel holes and a faint turquoise seam in the cracks. Tired, endless, never stops working, melancholic not evil. Colors: sandstone beige rock, soot brown timber, slate shadows, dull brass, amber lamp, tiny turquoise. Chunky readable pixel art, about 110 pixels wide and 85 tall sprite scaled up 8x with perfectly square pixel blocks. Background: completely flat solid magenta #ff00ff, no shadow, no floor, nothing else.
